summary: The v5 revision fixes most of the substantive presentation problems from my first screen. The abstract and highlights now match the numbers. Savings include recourse cost (23% and 11%), and the 41% point-planner success is reported. Non-identifiability is scoped to the error path in the abstract and highlights. The math rendering, glyphs and missing calibration-size grid are fixed, the figures are cut to 7, and the abstract is 238 words. Proposition 2 adds a formal link between compatible-set width and forecast error, but its proof assumes identical inputs while its statement allows tolerance-level differences, and the result is elementary. Unfilled author and affiliation placeholders still guarantee a technical return. Overclaims remain in the Conclusions, Section 4.7, the cover letter and the graphical abstract.

E4: savings now counted with recourse (23% and 11%)
E6 (partly): scoped in abstract, highlights and Introduction; not in Conclusions, cover letter or graphical abstract

issues.title: Author and affiliation placeholders still present (authors' choice)
issues.description: Elsevier's technical check returns any manuscript with an incomplete author list, affiliations or corresponding e-mail, whatever the scientific merit. The cover letter is signed 'on behalf of all authors' while only one author is named.
issues.evidence: manuscript_v5: '[Second author]b', '[Department, Institution, City, Country]' x2, '[e-mail]'; CRediT '[Second author]'; cover_letter_v5: '[Department, Institution, City, Country]', '[E-mail]'.
issues.corrective_action: Do not submit until the author list and affiliations are final, or submit as single-author with real affiliation and e-mail and remove the second-author CRediT line.

issues.title: Proposition 2 proof does not match its statement
issues.description: The statement defines M as models whose expected paths 'cannot be told apart from the observed path at the chosen tolerance'. Those paths differ within the tolerance, so a forecaster can receive different inputs. The proof assumes 'All models in M produce the same input to F'. As written, the bound holds only for exactly equal paths. In the stochastic setting it needs a Le Cam two-point (total-variation) argument, or a restatement for forecasters that are constant on tolerance-equivalence classes. The result is also an elementary triangle-inequality bound. Calling it a 'minimax lower bound' invites a theory reviewer to call it trivial, and it is not used numerically: Fig. 4c is not presented as the bound.
issues.corrective_action: Restate Proposition 2 for the noiseless or equivalence-class case and add one sentence on the noisy case, or label it a remark. Report half the compatible-set log-width as the per-pilot bound in Fig. 4c, and compare it with B-RPM and FLAT worst-case errors so that the result has empirical content.

issues.title: Residual overclaims in Conclusions, cover letter and graphical abstract
issues.description: The abstract and highlights were corrected, but other places still carry the earlier wording. This inconsistency is the kind of thing an editor checks.
issues.evidence: Conclusions: 'In our case study this kept its promised success rates even when the prior came from other application families' (72% vs 80% requested). Section 4.7: 'gives risk statements that hold', and 'A slope learned on soils misleads a fruit or fuel campaign' (no fuel task is in the 24-task case study). Cover letter: 'shows that the gain from more samples is not identifiable without prior information' (unscoped), 'the standard answer since Ali et al.', and no mention of Proposition 2. Graphical abstract: 'the gain is not identifiable from the pilot alone'. Conclusions: 'analyte signal and irreducible noise cannot be told apart' (unscoped).
issues.corrective_action: Use the abstract's scoped wording everywhere: 'came close to (72%/88% at requested 80%/90%)', 'from the pilot's error path', 'soil and fruit'. Update the cover letter's contribution list to include Proposition 2.

issues.title: Case study still not labelled exploratory
issues.description: The abstract presents the decision-calibrated planning result, with p < 0.001, as the main practical evidence. It was not among the pre-specified hypotheses HB1-HB4 (Section 3.6).
issues.evidence: Abstract Results; Section 3.6 'Campaign-planning case study'; Section 4.7.
issues.corrective_action: Add '(exploratory)' in the abstract and in Section 3.6, and note that cross-family calibration for the soil tasks rests on one mango task.

issues.title: Code 'available on request' (authors' choice)
issues.description: This is not a desk-reject trigger by itself. It does weaken the paper's central credibility claims (time-stamped pre-specification, one-command rerun, 'committed to the project repository'), and reviewers are likely to ask for public deposition.
issues.corrective_action: At least deposit the time-stamped protocol and addenda with a DOI (Zenodo or OSF), even if the code stays on request.

issues.title: Remaining cross-reference and numbering defects
issues.description: Several internal references are still broken.
issues.evidence: (i) Fig. 4b and 4c are cited before Fig. 3 in Section 4.3. (ii) Proposition 1 remark: 'in the numerical examples of Section 4.2', but Section 4.2 has no such examples. (iii) Section 4.9: ablation result referred to '(Section 2.4)'. (iv) Section 4.6: 'our earlier analysis identified' has no reference. (v) Fig. 4a uses n0 = 150 while the design and Fig. 4d use 200. (vi) Tables S1 (HB1/HB2) and S10 (HB4) and Figs S3-S7 are not cited in the main text; supplementary tables are not in citation order; Table S12 still has raw floats.
issues.corrective_action: Fix the citation order and dangling references, explain or align n0 = 150, and cite S1 and S10 where HB1, HB2 and HB4 are reported.

issues.title: Length claim does not match the count
issues.description: From Introduction to Conclusions, including captions and tables, the text is about 9,400 words (v4 was about 9,500 on the same count). The stated 7,800 presumably excludes captions and tables. The paper is still dense, with more than 15 method acronyms.
issues.corrective_action: Compress Sections 3.6, 4.8 and 4.9 and the forecaster list further. Aim for about 7,000 words of running text.

desk_decision: Technical return is certain while placeholders remain. Once they are filled, the paper is on balance sendable to review if N2-N4 are fixed; as is, it is borderline.
desk_reject_probability_note: 0.45 on substance with placeholders filled (down from 0.55); about 0.35 if the top 3 changes are made. The probability of a technical return as submitted is about 1.0.

top_changes.change: Fill in the author list, affiliations and e-mail, or submit as single-author and remove '[Second author]' from CRediT and 'all authors' from the cover letter.
top_changes.why: An automatic technical return; nothing else matters until this is fixed.

top_changes.change: Make every remaining claim match the abstract's scoped wording: Conclusions ('kept its promised success rates'), Section 4.7 ('risk statements that hold', 'fruit or fuel'), cover letter ('not identifiable', 'standard answer', add Proposition 2), graphical abstract ('not identifiable from the pilot alone'). Label the case study exploratory.
top_changes.why: Inconsistent claims across documents are an easy reason for an editor to reject.

top_changes.change: Repair Proposition 2: restate it for identical or equivalence-class inputs, or give a two-point argument for noisy paths. Show its empirical content by plotting half the compatible-set log-width as a per-pilot lower bound against the observed worst-case errors in Fig. 4c. Fix the Fig. 3/4 citation order and the dangling references.
top_changes.why: Proposition 2 is now the paper's strongest claim to a methodological development. A flawed proof undermines it, while a used and validated bound strengthens it.

recommendation: Return for technical corrections (placeholders). After correction and the top 3 changes, send to review.
